key.query: What studies compare early vs delayed surfactant treatment in preterm infants?

evidence.title: PubMed 22266202 [sections.0]
evidence.cited_text: The INSURE method, which consists of an intubation-surfactant-extubation sequence, is effective in reducing the need for mechanical ventilation (MV), the duration of respiratory support, and the need for surfactant replacement in preterm infants with respiratory distress syndrome

evidence.title: PubMed 19679893 [sections.0]
evidence.cited_text: In preterm infants with respiratory distress syndrome (RDS) nasal continuous positive airway pressure (nCPAP) with the "InSurE" procedure (intubation, surfactant, extubation) is increasingly used.

evidence.title: PubMed 17476269 [sections.0]
evidence.cited_text: a method for surfactant administration by transient intubation, INSURE (i.e. INtubation SURfactant Extubation) during nasal continuous positive airway pressure (nCPAP) for moderately preterm infants with respiratory distress syndrome (RDS)
